name: Christopher S Kiper
current_role: Co-founder, Managing Director & Chief Investment Officer, Legion Partners Asset Management; director, Lifecore Biomedical (since 2023)
profile: Christopher Kiper co-founded Legion Partners (Los Angeles, 2012), a long-only activist fund targeting North American small caps with fewer than 15 concentrated positions. His wealth tracks Legion's activist stakes, including a 10%+ holding in Lifecore Biomedical, where he sits on the board as Legion's representative. He has also served on boards such as NN Inc.
interesting_fact: Legion describes its method as a 'private equity approach to investing in public equities', running a concentrated book of fewer than 15 small-cap positions and engaging boards directly.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Legion he worked at Shamrock Capital, the Disney family's investment firm. On the Beyond the Boardroom podcast he said 'most boards need upgrading' and that replacing directors is one of the biggest ways to change a company.
notes: Activist investor, not an operator, but a good fit for small-cap governance/value angles. Clear Channel Outdoor's 2024 Legion board seat went to co-founder Ted White, and I could not confirm Kiper sat on the CCO board, so the SEC-derived CCO directorship may be a data error. CCO was later taken private by Mubadala. Reach him through Legion's general inbox.

name: Gerhard Watzinger
current_role: Chairman of the Board, CrowdStrike (since April 2012)
profile: German-born security executive who has chaired CrowdStrike since its 2012 founding. He was CEO of encryption company SafeBoot until McAfee bought it in 2007 for about $350M, then became McAfee's Chief Strategy Officer and EVP. He also sits on the boards of KnowBe4, NinjaOne and Invicti.
interesting_fact: At McAfee he was the architect of the company's $7.7B sale to Intel, before teaming up with McAfee colleagues George Kurtz and Dmitri Alperovitch at CrowdStrike.
deep_cut_fact: He ran SafeBoot, a Dutch-based data-encryption company that McAfee bought for about $350M in 2007, then took over McAfee's new Data Protection business unit and reported to CEO Dave DeWalt. He has an advanced computer-science degree from the University of Applied Sciences in Munich.
notes: Low public profile: he gives few interviews and I found no personal social accounts. The only published route is CrowdStrike corporate communications.

name: Anthony D. Fassino
current_role: Retired Group President, Construction Industries, Caterpillar (retired May 31, 2026); 2025-26 chair of ARTBA
profile: Tony Fassino spent about 30 years at Caterpillar, running Building Construction Products (2018) and then the Construction Industries segment as group president (2021 to early 2026). Earlier he was a senior vice president in the Oil & Gas and Electrification & Energy Solutions divisions. His wealth comes from Caterpillar stock and equity compensation. He handed the segment to Rod Shurman on Feb 1, 2026 and retired May 31, 2026.
interesting_fact: He was elected 2025-26 chair of the American Road & Transportation Builders Association (ARTBA), after several years as a volunteer vice chair. As chair he pushed for practical approaches to Buy America expansion and OSHA's proposed heat rule.
deep_cut_fact: He is a Bradley University mechanical engineer (bachelor's and master's), studying in Peoria, Caterpillar's longtime hometown. Before running construction equipment, he led Cat's Electrification & Energy Solutions division, which is directly relevant to an energy/data-center podcast (Cat gensets power data centers).
notes: Retired from Caterpillar in 2026, so corporate channels may no longer reach him. ARTBA may be a better route while his chair term runs. His energy-solutions background suits the data-center power angle. Some outlets say he joined Cat in 1997 rather than 1996.

name: Sheela Kosaraju
current_role: Executive Vice President & Chief Legal Officer, Ciena Corporation
profile: Sheela Kosaraju has been at Ciena, the optical networking company, since 2010. She rose from international general counsel and head of international legal to SVP & General Counsel (2023), also served as acting Chief People Officer from August 2023, and now signs filings as EVP & Chief Legal Officer. Her wealth is Ciena equity, which has risen sharply as AI data-center bandwidth demand lifted the stock.
interesting_fact: She leads legal at a company now positioned as 'the global leader in high-speed connectivity' for the AI era. In fiscal Q3 2026 two customers made up 41.7% of Ciena's revenue, a sign of how concentrated hyperscaler demand has become.
deep_cut_fact: Before Ciena she was general counsel at two early-stage companies, HomeCom Communications and Closedloop Solutions. For a time she ran Ciena's legal and people (HR) functions at once, as SVP & General Counsel and acting Chief People Officer.
notes: Corporate legal executive with little public profile. Ciena's site blocks automated fetches, so I couldn't confirm a press email; contact Ciena corporate communications through ciena.com. Ciena (optical interconnect for AI data centers) is highly relevant to the podcast's themes. Web search budget ran out at this point, so research relied on SEC filings.

name: Kimberly Alexy
current_role: Founder & principal, Alexy Capital Management; independent director and Audit Committee chair, Western Digital; director, Netskope
profile: Kimberly E. Alexy, a CFA, was an equity research VP at Lehman Brothers (1995-98) and a senior VP and managing director at Prudential Securities (1998-2003). She founded the private investment fund Alexy Capital Management in 2005. She has been a professional public-company director at tech firms including Western Digital (since 2018), Sandisk, Netskope, Five9, Mandiant and Alteryx.
interesting_fact: As Western Digital's Audit Committee chair she leads oversight of the company's enterprise risk management program, at a storage maker now at the center of AI data-center demand. She also served on the board of the spun-off Sandisk.
deep_cut_fact: Unusually for a finance-trained director, she holds a CERT Certificate in Cybersecurity Oversight for corporate directors, issued by the CERT Division of Carnegie Mellon's Software Engineering Institute. That fits her board seats at security firms Mandiant and Netskope.
notes: Professional board director with a low media profile. The proxy no longer lists Sandisk as a current board, so she appears to have left it. The only published route is through Western Digital IR. Strong fit for a data-storage/AI-infrastructure governance angle.
